podcast.title: Fatal Drunk Driving Incident (2013)
podcast.body: In 2013, Todd Harrell, the bassist for Three Doors Down, was driving drunk and high on OxyContin and other prescription drugs when his speeding car caused the death of a truck driver. This was his second drunk driving conviction. "In 2013, he was driving drunk and high on oxy and other prescription drugs when his speeding car resulted in the death of a truck driver."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Most Dangerous Artists in Rock

podcast.title: Ongoing Legal Troubles (2014, 2018)
podcast.body: Harrell continued to face legal issues, including another DUI charge in 2014 and being caught sending drugs to friends in prison. In 2018, police responding to a domestic disturbance call at his home found drugs and guns, violating his release conditions and leading to a 10-year sentence with the Mississippi Department of Corrections. "There was another DUI charge in 2014, and then Herrell was caught sending drugs to buddies in prison."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: CBGB Gig and Record Deal
podcast.body: A performance at the legendary CBGB club in New York attracted the attention of Republic Records, a subsidiary of Universal Music, which subsequently signed them to a deal. "A gig at CBGB got the attention of Republic Records, a subsidiary of Universal Music, and they signed them to a deal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Big Bands from Small Towns

podcast.title: Continuing Career
podcast.body: Despite some tailing off in sales after their initial success, Three Doors Down has remained together, continuing to release albums and tour. "Things tailed off a little bit after that, but the band is still together and they're still releasing albums and still touring."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Escatawpa, Mississippi Origins - Population 3,566
podcast.body: Three Doors Down formed in Escatawpa, Mississippi, a town of 3,566 people located on the Gulf Coast along Interstate 10, in an area referred to as the "Redneck Riviera." "Way down in Southern Mississippi, right on the Gulf Coast along Interstate 10, an area called, and I'm not making this up, the Redneck Riviera, is the town of Escatapa. It's east of Bloc Sea, west of Mobile, Alabama, south of Haddie's Burg, and part of the area around Pascagula. This is where you'll find three doors down."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation Out of Boredom
podcast.body: The band formed in 1996 seemingly out of a lack of other activities, with things surprisingly going well and leading them to record original material. "They were formed in 1996 because they really had nothing better to do, but things went surprisingly well and they decided to record some original material."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Guitarist Matt Roberts' Death
podcast.body: Original guitarist Matt Roberts, who had left the band in 2012, tragically died of an overdose in 2016. "Originally, the guitarist Matt Roberts died of an overdose in 2016. He'd left the band in 2012."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Incarceration and Expulsion from Band
podcast.body: Harrell served a year in jail for the fatal accident. Due to this being his second drunk driving conviction, he was also removed from Three Doors Down. "He spent a year in jail, and since that was the second drunk driving conviction, he was also kicked out of the band."

podcast.title: Reputation Spread to New York
podcast.body: After their local radio hit, the band's reputation quickly spread throughout the region and then up the East Coast, reaching New York City. "After that, their reputation spread throughout the region and then up the east coast all the way to New York."

xref.title: Beatles Producer Death in 2016
xref.body: George Martin, the renowned producer for The Beatles, was among the notable music industry figures who died in 2016, a year characterized by significant losses of musical icons. "David Bowie, Prince, Glen Fry of the Eagles, two members of the Jefferson Airplane, Matt Roberts of Three Doors Down, George Michael, Beatles producer George Martin, Keith Emerson and Greg Lake of Emerson, like in Palmer, Maurice White of Earth Wind and Fire and dozens more."
